**Finding: Compliant (preferred position)** — no redline proposed.

The agreement contains no non-solicitation, no-poach, or no-hire covenant binding Meridian Fieldworks. I confirmed this by reading both planner candidate sections and running full-text searches for "solicit", "employ", "hire", "induce", and "recruit" — the only hits are § 12.3 (favourable to us), an employment-law reference in the "Applicable Law" definition, and employer's-liability insurance in § 18.1.

This satisfies our preferred position outright, so there is no need to fall back to a narrowed mutual non-solicit. Section 12.3 in fact goes further in our favour, expressly preserving our freedom to hire anyone responding to general recruitment and recording that we have made no no-hire commitment — language that benefits us and should be defended if Copperleaf proposes to trim it.

One adjacent point worth flagging to the deal team, though outside this rule: § 12.4 imposes a 24-month post-term non-compete on us ("Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory"). That is a competition/exclusivity restriction rather than a personnel non-solicit, and it also sits in direct tension with § 12.3's statement that we have made no non-compete commitment. I have not flagged it here to avoid double-counting, but it should be picked up under the restrictive-covenant/exclusivity rule (alongside § 2.1's take-or-pay and § 2.2's sole-provider commitment).
